questions.q: Per this lesson, what is an Oracle instance actually made of?
options: Background processes plus shared memory (the SGA), existing only while the instance is started
The physical datafiles and control files stored on disk
A synonym Oracle uses for what SQL Server calls a database
A single configuration file that defines connection settings
questions.explain: The instance is running processes and RAM (the SGA) — it has no persistent on-disk form of its own.

questions.q: What is an Oracle database, as distinct from an instance, per this lesson?
options: The physical datafiles, control files, and redo log files on disk, which persist whether or not an instance is running
The same thing as an instance, just a different name for it
A logical grouping of SQL Server-style filegroups
A background process that manages memory allocation
questions.explain: The database is data at rest on disk — datafiles, control files, and redo logs — independent of any running instance.

questions.q: Why does Oracle Real Application Clusters (RAC) demonstrate that an instance and a database are genuinely separate things?
options: RAC lets multiple instances on different servers mount and open the same single database at the same time
RAC eliminates the need for a database entirely
RAC merges multiple databases into a single instance
RAC only works when instance and database are the exact same object
questions.explain: RAC only makes sense because multiple separate instances can connect to one shared database — proving they aren't the same thing.

questions.q: In Oracle's multitenant architecture (the default since Oracle Database 12c), what is a Pluggable Database (PDB)?
options: A database that looks self-contained to applications but shares its instance and SGA with other PDBs inside the same CDB
A completely separate instance with its own dedicated memory
A backup copy of the root container
A deprecated feature no longer used in current Oracle versions
questions.explain: PDBs appear self-contained to the applications connecting to them, but multiple PDBs share the same CDB's instance, background processes, and SGA.

questions.q: What holds the shared metadata common to all pluggable databases in a Container Database?
options: The root container, CDB$ROOT
Each individual PDB, independently
The SGA's redo log buffer
The Oracle Universal Installer
questions.explain: CDB$ROOT is the root container of a CDB and holds Oracle's shared metadata and common users used across the whole container.
